speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond this, Mr Tan Wu Meng and other Members have also asked about our on-going efforts to enhance support for seniors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our care landscape, we launched the new Community Care Apartments in Bukit Batok last month – a novel public housing-cum-care concept.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The flats integrate senior-friendly housing features with care services and community building through social interaction and communal spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When I visited the exhibition at HDB Hub, a senior told me that she had been long awaiting this!

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Others said they appreciated the communal spirit that it brings, greater assurance to age independently and the range of programmes to keep them active.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to work with MND on planning for additional sites.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last December, we announced a new Eldercare Centre service to serve all seniors nationwide.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These centres would be key nodes in our social support and care landscape, and the first batch of centres will start from 1 May 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Each will provide a common suite of “ABC” services – A for Active ageing programmes, B for Befriending, and C – connecting to Care services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Seniors can participate in wellness activities or have their queries about care services and support schemes answered.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Befrienders will reach out to those with little support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To better reflect the new model, centres that provide the suite of “ABC” services will be named “Active Ageing Centres”.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, some centres provide care services, such as day care and community rehabilitation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They will be called “Active Ageing Care Hubs” once they come on board to provide the new “ABC” services on top of their existing regular care services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Next, on care-givers – they play a key role in supporting seniors to age well in the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To support them better, MOH launched the Caregiver Support Action Plan (CSAP) two years ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we launched the Home Caregiving Grant two years ago, providing a cash grant to help with care-giving costs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Yip Hon Weng's query, we are also reviewing the Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund to further defray costs of care-giving.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we set up touchpoints within the community to support seniors and their care-givers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, the Silver Generation Office refers frail and homebound seniors to the Medical Escort and Transport service to assist them in getting to their medical appointments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, we also have various care-giver respite services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We introduced the home-based respite care pilot in September 2019 for palliative cancer patients and expanded this in 2021 to all patients receiving home palliative care, regardless of diagnosis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Fourth, we will be launching a new grant, a new grant call this year on the Caregiving Ecosystem, under the National Innovation Challenge on Active and Confident Ageing, to support research on innovative solutions to sustainable care-giving.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Fifth, we have worked with community partners to set up four care-giver community outreach teams to better support care-givers at risk of burn-out or developing mental health needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will increase this to six teams by year-end.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also established seven care-giver support networks in Dementia-Friendly Communities, enabling peer support among care-givers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, we will pilot a structured support system for care-givers of loved ones first diagnosed with dementia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will proactively support and equip these persons with dementia and their care-givers with information upon the first diagnosis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will also share more on the support measures we have for care-givers of Persons with Disabilities in my MSF COS speech.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To better serve seniors’ needs, we have expanded the capacity of community care services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We share Mr Ang Wei Neng’s concern about the impact of COVID-19 on the construction of nursing homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To mitigate this, we are working with providers to open up currently non-operational beds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: AIC also helps seniors and care-givers with alternative care arrangements while awaiting nursing home placement, such as the Interim Caregiver Service for short-term home-based custodial care, and the Integrated Home and Day Care programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Seniors or care-givers who need help can approach AIC for further assistance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Before I conclude, let me summarise my speech in Malay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):    The healthcare system is critical in building a cohesive social support system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to transform it to provide proactive and inclusive healthcare for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, even as we continue the fight against COVID-19, MOH’s key priority continues to be a healthcare system that provides good quality, affordable and sustainable healthcare for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will speak on how deepening our partnerships with the private sector, strengthening our healthcare financing system, driving greater value in healthcare delivery, and uplifting our healthcare workforce can help us to achieve these aims.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our strong partnerships with the private sector over the years have allowed us to mount a robust and coordinated national response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, we have partnered private hospitals to provide subsidised care to patients, such as Raffles Hospital for non-life-threatening emergency cases, an example referenced by Ms Mariam Jafaar, as well as Parkway Hospital, Mt Alvenia and Farrer Park Hospitals for other conditions, including dengue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Private providers also supported our Community Care Facilities, clinics in worker dormitories, roving medical or swabbing teams, and many much more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our partnerships with private GPs have also matured over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, over two million Singaporeans can access subsidised primary care at CHAS GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: GP clinics in Primary Care Networks (PCNs) anchored care in the community, deriving economies of scale for ancillary services, and serving 130,000 patients with chronic conditions last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In the long-term care sector, private nursing homes receive funding to provide subsidised services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Both private and not-for-profit organisations also operate many Government-built nursing homes and eldercare centres, under a Build-Own-Lease arrangement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In the pandemic, they actively stepped up safe management measures and supported COVID-19 testing and vaccinations to keep our seniors safe.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To mount a strong pandemic response, MOH also tapped on expertise and resources from private laboratories for PCR testing capacity, vendors and distributors of medical supplies, cleaning companies that disinfected our medical facilities, and security companies, facility managers and transport companies that supported our quarantine and other operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: There are too many to list comprehensively, but each one helped make our robust national response to COVID-19 possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On behalf of all Singaporeans, I thank our many private-sector partners for protecting Singaporeans from the scourge of COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I, therefore, agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar that the Government should continue to renew and deepen our partnership with private healthcare providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we will uplift capabilities of our GPs through continuing professional education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE)’s Clinical Update Service (CUES) assists GPs in navigating areas of uncertainty and challenges specific to their area of practice through personalised, evidence-based discussions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also train and equip GPs to care for persons with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: My colleague, Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, will share more on this later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, strengthening regulatory frameworks, such as the Healthcare Services Act (HCSA) passed in January last year, will help us to better regulate newer, non-premises-based, models of care, such as telemedicine, through a services-based licensing framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Fee benchmarks, an area which Dr Tan Yia Swam mentioned earlier, was introduced in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This gave patients seeking care at private sector providers more confidence that charges are fair and reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Early data showed that doctors have been taking reference from the benchmarks, with more than 80% of charges in 2019 within the upper limit of the benchmarks, and this is about 4% higher than in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Therefore, together with the Fee Benchmarks Advisory Committee, we introduced new benchmarks for anaesthetist and inpatient attendance charges in December 2020 and will continue to review and develop new areas of fee benchmarking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I will now move on to our healthcare financing system which is anchored on Government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, the Government provides significant subsidies, covering up to 80% of treatment costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a society, we widely accept the need to be progressive and to target subsidies to those with greater needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When formulating subsidy levels across the various healthcare settings, we should also encourage right-siting of care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will, therefore, introduce a set of changes to the subsidy frameworks for inpatient care at the acute hospitals, specialist outpatient clinics (SOCs) and community hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For inpatient admissions to acute hospitals, we currently use individual income as the basis for means-testing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I have seen in my clinical practice and also met people during my Meet-The-People sessions, how a sole breadwinner may earn a high individual income, but shoulders the full responsibility for his or her household needs alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For such individuals, healthcare costs can become a significant strain, and I have great sympathy for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Per Capita Household Income (PCHI), which is already widely used in our healthcare system, is, therefore, a better measure of means, as it also considers the amount of household support available, and the number of household members that this individual supports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another observation over the years is that the physical differences between B2 and C wards are no longer so obvious, following infrastructural improvements to raise patient safety and infection control standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, we still have a legacy system of using choice of wards as a proxy of financial means to differentiate subsidy levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Currently, B2 wards are subsidised at 50% to 65% and C-class wards at 65% to 80%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This acute inpatient subsidy framework will also be applied to day surgeries which are currently subsidised at 65%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Effectively, this will increase subsidies for 70% of day surgery bills and encourage day surgeries instead of inpatient admissions when appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Overall, with MediShield Life and MediSave, we expect that most patients will not see a change in out-of-pocket payments, or OOP payments, with about 30% seeing lower OOP and about 15% seeing higher OOP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While we raised SOC subsidies for the lower income up to 70% in 2014, higher income patients and median-income patients currently receive the same 50% subsidy support, despite both having quite different financial means.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For a family of four, these PCHI levels correspond to household incomes of $13,200 and $26,000 respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless, these higher income households may continue to tap on MediSave up to the applicable withdrawal limits to help pay for healthcare bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With the introduction of the CHAS Green tier in 2019, higher PCHI patients with chronic conditions also have access to subsidised chronic care at CHAS GP clinics as an alternative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Complex chronic patients who are not suitable for management at primary care will also be able to utilise their MediSave through higher limits that are going to be introduced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Some preferred air-conditioning and others wanted more privacy in the private wards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the cost of a potentially long tail of SOC consultations upon discharge worries them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For this reason, some patients have sometimes had to forgo their preference and request for a subsidised ward instead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These particular groups are those that Dr Tan Yia Swam shared earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With better targeted subsidies at the SOCs, we will now allow private patients in the Inpatient setting to opt for either subsidised or private SOC for their discharge follow up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: If subsidised SOC is chosen, the patient will no longer be able to pick their specialist, as is the current practice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Overall, the SOC subsidy changes will affect about 30% of subsidised SOC patients, who are from higher PCHI households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Of these, seven in 10 will see an increase of less than $100 in total co-payment for their cumulative annual bills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This can be further offset by MediSave or MediShield Life, or for those who have private insurance coverage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For elderly patients, any increase in co-payment will also be partially offset by Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having worked in an acute surgical ward, I have occasionally encountered patients who have recovered significantly to be well enough for discharge to a community hospital for sub-acute or rehabilitative care, but who were reluctant to do so, due to the differences in the subsidy levels between acute and community hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will, therefore, enhance subsidies available in our community hospitals to support patients in utilising appropriate care, and facilitate the smooth flow of patients from acute hospitals to community hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Together with increased MediShield Life claim limits for community hospitals sub-acute care from 1 March 2021, this should make community hospitals even more affordable, especially when compared to a prolonged acute hospital stay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Almost all, about 95% of all community hospitals patients will see an increase in subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, subsidies are the bedrock of our healthcare financing system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Healthcare costs will continue to rise in the years ahead, and Government spending on healthcare subsidies will commensurately increase even after all these changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition to these changes, MOH will also review the financing landscape in the Long-Term Care, or LTC, sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last year, we launched CareShield Life and Medisave Care, improving affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, as we uplift standards and draw in more Singaporeans to work in the LTC sector, cost pressures may potentially impact affordability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, in anticipation of these challenges, we will once again review the financing situation for the LTC sector to see if further changes are needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Next, I will speak on the enhancements to MediShield Life and MediSave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, MediShield Life covers Singaporeans for large hospitalisation bills and selected costly outpatient treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Premiums will also be adjusted to keep the scheme solvent and sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Premium payment will also be deferred till the end 2021 for those who have insufficient MediSave balances and are unable to pay their premiums due to the economic impact from COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As noted by Mr Gerald Giam, the benefit changes and premium adjustments will take effect on or after 1 March 2021, which is the Monday that just passed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On premium pricing, I wish to assure Mr Gerald Giam that the pricing assumptions are assessed by independent actuarial experts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are studying how technically complex actuarial reports can be shared in a meaningful way, and will provide an update when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, MediSave helps Singaporeans set aside some income towards their future healthcare needs, such as co-payments for large bills and for health insurance premiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Hazel Poa and Mr Gerald Giam asked how MediSave coverage can be expanded in the outpatient setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We certainly recognise that seniors tend to have higher healthcare expenses, especially if they have chronic conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: From the start of this year, we raised annual MediSave limits from $500 to $700 for patients with complex chronic conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme, or CDMP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The list of CDMP conditions will be reviewed regularly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To support elderly patients in seeking outpatient treatment, we also introduced Flexi-MediSave in 2015, and lowered the age eligibility from 65 to 60 in 2018, allowing more patients to benefit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to review the MediSave withdrawal limits regularly, to ensure that they remain relevant and adequate for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond healthcare financing, as Dr Lim Wee Kiak has pointed out, we must also control upstream growth in medical costs to ensure affordability in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we should tap on technology to deliver care more effectively while optimising our limited manpower resource.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Since the circuit breaker period, polyclinics, SOCs and community nursing teams have used teleconsultation to reach their patients at home, allowing continued consultation and advice for these patients during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I understand from feedback that patients are comfortable with teleconsultation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Further, when ready, the National Central Fill Pharmacy will consolidate medications across multiple providers in a central location, enabling the delivery of medications directly to patient's homes, secured post boxes or other convenient locations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will improve the access to pharmacy services, including for seniors with mobility needs, as Dr Tan Wu Meng mentioned, and support new care models, such as telemedicine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also agree with Dr Tan Wu Meng that patient navigators can improve patient convenience, and our public healthcare institutions have increased the number of staff trained in such roles by 3% annually between 2018 and 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But beyond this, we have also improved scheduling services and offer telehealth follow-ups for suitable patients, helping to reduce the need for multiple hospital visits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, innovative care models have been introduced to improve right-siting of care in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Examples include the Urgent Care Centre (UCC) pilot concept and the GPFirst Pilot Programme which support patients with non-emergency conditions, helping them avoid unnecessary emergency department visits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOH will review the performance of such technology-enabled services and innovative care models, and explore how we can scale up the promising ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also strive for greater value and better services in our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE) helps us to ensure that the prices we pay for subsidised treatments and vaccines are fair and commensurate with the healthcare outcomes they confer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is done through health technology assessments and value-based pricing (VBP) negotiations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: ACE will continue to ensure that subsidised medicines and medical technologies are both clinically and cost-effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also established ALPS in 2018 to aggregate demand and achieve economies of scale in procurement and supply chain management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: ALPS will study how this CWD concept can be expanded to the whole of public healthcare boosting efficiency, resilience, and value in our healthcare supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also agree with Ms Ng Ling Ling that funding mechanisms can drive greater value through influencing providers’ behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We, in fact, implemented some of the ideas that she has shared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This gives providers the opportunity to optimise care, reduce costs, and pass on savings to patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will expand these positive efforts and study other financing solutions and innovations that encourage healthcare providers to optimise care and improve outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond technology and care models, healthcare is ultimately a high touch and people-centric sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Healthcare professionals are key in improving patient care and outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: COVID-19 has shown us the importance of maintaining a resilient core of healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Going forward, we plan to develop the Corps into a platform for citizen engagement and volunteerism in healthcare during peacetime, and serve as a reserve pool in times of crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: COVID-19 has been a trying time for all our healthcare staff and volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I know many staff in our public healthcare institutions suspended their annual leave to meet the surge in manpower demands during the height of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many have played a critical role in the battle against COVID-19 and I would like to express our heartfelt thanks to all of them for their dedication and contributions, and their families for supporting them through this very tough period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also recognise and appreciate the contributions of our outsourced workers in the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We agree with Dr Tan Wu Meng that their work is intrinsic to the hospital as many of them, such as cleaners and health attendants, work alongside our healthcare staff in the wards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The intent of outsourcing is to leverage economies of scale and enable our public healthcare institutions to focus on the core mission of delivery of healthcare services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: While our public healthcare institutions are not their direct employers, they have also extended support and tokens of appreciation to these outsourced workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to work closely with the outsourced companies to improve the work conditions of their staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To strengthen our healthcare workforce, I agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar that we need to attract more talent to healthcare and to build a strong local core.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we have strengthened our pipeline of fresh graduates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: At steady state, we will be training about 3,300 students annually in our Institutes of Higher Learning to become healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Second, we have built pathways for progression, and continue to expand mid-career conversion pipelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We introduced new pathways for Enrolled Nurses to move from Nitec to Diploma-level qualifications within a shorter time and progress as a Registered Nurse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In line with the recommendations of the Future Nursing Career Review Committee (FNCRC), we enhanced nursing career tracks and job scopes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nurses can now perform a wider breadth of care tasks and make clinical decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are seeing increased interest in our Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This year, Ngee Ann Polytechnic (NP) will join Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) in offering the two-year accelerated PCP for diploma-level registered nurses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also explore more pathways for mid-career entrants to complete their training in a shorter time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) is introducing an accelerated PCP in Occupational Therapy for those who have already got a degree in a science-related field.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They can complete their training in slightly under three years instead of four years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Third, we actively partner healthcare employers in re-designing jobs for staff working in healthcare support and operations support roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, the Care Support Associate (CSA) role in SGH, and AIC’s sectoral job redesign project relook processes and blend clinical support, administrative and operations responsibilities into new roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These initiatives encourage cross-deployment and multi-skilling of staff, create new career pathways, and provide interesting development opportunities for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our healthcare workforce is the lifeblood of our healthcare system and the work that they do is critical in protecting the health and safety of our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must maintain the salary competitiveness of healthcare staff against the overall market to attract and retain quality talent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Aside from salaries, we will also work with healthcare providers and union partners to make healthcare a progressive and fulfilling career.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With deeper partnerships with our private sector providers, innovative, value-based healthcare delivery, a strong healthcare financing framework, and a resilient healthcare workforce, we will be better placed to provide all Singaporeans with good quality, affordable, and accessible healthcare.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Chairman, in my recent speeches, I spoke about the importance of mental health and the need to destigmatise mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Now, its frequency has reached to a point where my students have given me hashtag DWR4MH, which means "Do what's right for mental health." Chairman, we need to change the negative perception and treat mental health issues like any other health conditions.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Additionally, it is crucial for those who need assistance are able to get them quickly and properly.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Tan, if you like to take both your cuts together, please do.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce convened by the MOH and the IMH in October 2020, with representatives from various Ministries has done great work in promoting mental health literacy.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Yet, I hear of anecdotal cases of discrimination against people who have mental illnesses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: I will speak on three main groups: one, the general population and working adults; two, the young; three, other vulnerable groups.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For the general public, how do we react when we see someone behaving “oddly” – such as talking to themselves, removing all their clothing in public, becoming violent for no apparent reason, or wailing inconsolably?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Do we take a video and post the incident online?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Or will we step forward to offer some kind of help?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: I suspect many people want to, but we do not feel able to.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For working adults, I understand when colleagues and bosses see only the underperformance of the affected employee.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For example, frequent absenteeism, missing work deadlines, or simply being very unsociable at work.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Physical illnesses such as high blood pressure and diabetes, have a measurable scale of normality.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Is it triggered by something specific and situational which will resolve itself after the event is over?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Or could these bad moods be symptoms of a mental illness such as depression, anxiety disorder or even schizophrenia?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: We need to have more schemes in place for the general population to recognise early signs of mental illnesses and learn how to assist as a first responder.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Regarding the youth, the world is changing fast.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: I am only a few years past the official definition of "youth", but there are times when I feel very distant from them!

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Exploring one’s sense of identity as a growing teenager has never been easy.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Being in a more connected world now, they are perhaps subject to more pressures.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: How do we recognise and stop bullying of any kind – physical, emotional, verbal?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: In my Budget speech, I brought up the modern phenomenon of cyberbullying and the amplification effect of social media.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: A short video clip gets shared, liked and goes viral.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: When I was a child, any once-off silly act gets forgotten, and maybe brought up only at annual family gatherings during Chinese New Year.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Suicide is a painful and difficult subject, as there is a taboo around this.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: But this is exactly why healthcare has to educate and teach about the mental health issues that contribute to this tragedy.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Let us guide our people to be more caring, and inclusive.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: How do we approach those who are different?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For many of the patients with mental illnesses, it is a lifelong disease, and some of the triggers may be related to socio-economic stressors.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Young patients with mental health may just be the tip of the iceberg, and further investigation may uncover more members of the family with mental health issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: They will all need to have adequate treatment.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Community support has to come in hand in hand with doctors in the hospital to provide integrated care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: The network of support is essential to minimise the episodes and severity of relapses.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Focus cannot be just on the acute admissions, but in discharge back to the community, gainful employment and meaningful living.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Does the Ministry have plans in place to help these groups?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: In summary, the global COVID-19 pandemic has caused increased stress in multiple areas – retrenchment, change in jobs, lifestyles, education.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Many people are now working from home due to COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: Other speakers have shared on the challenges that parents with young children face working from home.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: While some adults have managed to incorporate daily exercise into their new routine, many others are struggling to balance work, daily chores and the demands of family care.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For many busy working parents, the daily commute to work and back home might be the only exercise they get.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For example, walking 10 minutes to the MRT station and another 10 minutes to the workplace.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: This makes up a total of 40 minutes' walking time and one may clock 8,000 to 10,000 steps, hopefully.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: The lack of commute while working from home means a reduction in mobility.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: For those of us who like to chat over coffee or lunch at the office, working from home also results in less social engagement, which may lead to chronic health issues such as obesity, depression and anxiety.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam
text: What are the Ministry's plans to support Singaporeans to pursue healthy habits in this new norm?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak, if you would like to take both your cuts together, please do.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Mr Chairman, nowadays, we see everyone wearing a healthcare device to monitor our steps, our heartrate, our stress level, oxygen saturation and how well we slept last night.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Some of the more advanced ones perform electrocardiogram (ECG) and even measure your blood sugar levels now as well as blood pressure.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: On our home front, I am encouraged to read about the Health Promotion Board and Fitbit – headquartered in San Francisco, California – tap on technology to help Singaporeans to live healthier using its devices.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I must commend the Ministry for mobilising technology to boost Singaporeans' interest in fitness and healthcare.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I envisage in the near future, I will have access to my own medical as well as health record, just like the details of my COVID-19 vaccinations on HealthHub app now.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: In the near future, I will receive a reminder from MOH for my annual health checks, blood tests, annual immunisation, and my once-in-five-years colonoscopy screening.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Once completed, there could be an artificial intelligence (AI) system in MOH that will review my health records, and then they will send me an advice to take active steps to improve my health through lifestyle adjustments.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: They may recalculate and lower my annual MediShield insurance premium, if my health is good.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: That will encourage more Singaporeans to come on board and to take responsibility of their own health.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I feel we can go a step further now to get Singaporeans to do more exercises, to manage their stress, maintain mental wellbeing and manage their sleep better.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Another area would be to manage good nutritional diet daily and influence them to have good eating habits.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I urge MOH to take advantage of all the advances in digital healthcare devices now to set up a national health management system and to step up the partnership with Singaporeans to achieve good health for life.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: One of the things that comes out from this COVID-19 pandemic is the heightened public awareness about the role of immunisation in our healthcare measures.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Immunisation is one of the key advances in medicine that has extended the lifespan of humans globally.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Apart from the immunisations that we received during our childhood, many Singaporeans do not get regular immunisations unless they need to travel or for work.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How many Singaporeans would regularly go for their annual flu vaccinations or pneumococcal vaccinations?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Even new vaccines such as the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine will reduce the risk of cervical cancer.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We are constantly reminded to take our COVID-19 vaccination to protect our loved ones, especially those immuno-compromised and the elderly around us.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Likewise, we should do the same for influenza.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State for Health Dr Janil Puthucheary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, Singapore is fortunate to have a workforce in the healthcare family driven by professionalism and dedication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our people answered the call of duty, they have carried us far in this fight against COVID-19 and have contributed to keeping Singapore safe during the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our infectious diseases experts and staff at the National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID) and other public healthcare institutions have worked to provide clinical guidance to and support for public health operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Laboratory specialists at the National Public Health Laboratory provided guidance for COVID-19 tests and conducted genomic analysis to support cluster investigations and surveillance for variants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The staff at the public and private healthcare institutions do their duty, putting themselves in harm's way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They undertake healthcare operations in high-risk locations like the foreign workers' dormitories, emergency departments, hospital wards and intensive care units across our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I echo the sentiments of many in the House to express our deep appreciation for colleagues in many, many different roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NCID was one of several initiatives and projects that came out of the lessons we learned from SARS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the test of that crisis, we identified vulnerabilities and in our response, developed capabilities and institutions that exist to this day, like NCID, helping us with COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In this crisis, we are learning new lessons and responding to different vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to institutionalise the capabilities that we are developing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have needed to deal with the pandemic and continue the usual clinical services and, now, stand up a massive national vaccination exercise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many of these skills, tools, processes and systems we have developed are distributed across our healthcare network and the care providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But centrally, at MOH, we have had to also develop and improve our organisational capability to manage the response to this crisis and, hopefully, be better prepared for the next.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have worked hard, in collaboration with other Ministries and other agencies, to coordinate COVID-19-related operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a capability and a team that we will need in order to be better prepared for the next pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are heartened by the appreciation demonstrated by the public for our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, today, there are still cases of harassment and abuse against staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This has affected their well-being and their safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Public healthcare institutions also have policies in place to handle abuse cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The institutions conduct training for healthcare staff, including on de-escalation measures during potential conflict and abuse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, we will work with the clusters and the Healthcare Services Employees' Union (HSEU) on a tripartite effort to strengthen messages against abuse and harassment of public healthcare staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: During the Budget debate, Mr Darryl David asked about staff benefits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Wan Rizal also asked about this just recently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our public healthcare institutions do pay close attention to staff leave and make time for sufficient rest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are planned to ensure sufficient staffing for patient safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are also rostered breaks and staff rotations to ensure sufficient rest during and between shifts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The committee will share best practices and provide feedback to MOH on possible enhancements to improve staff wellbeing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Besides healthcare workers, our HealthTech – health technology – engineers have also played an important role.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have rapidly developed systems to support new operational demands, including the on-going vaccination operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These are also important capabilities that we need within our system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thus, to grow our health technology workforce, we work closely with the Integrated Health Information Systems (IHiS) to redesign jobs and actively recruit people into new roles, including software engineers, systems analysts and cybersecurity professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To facilitate mid-career switches into HealthTech, IHiS, Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and SkillsFuture have curated specific training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One such example of a mid-career switch is a gentleman by the name of Mr Daniel Ong, whom I spoke to recently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He was a copywriter and his formal education was in English Literature.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He could not write code before joining IMDA's Tech Immersion and Placement Programme, which is part of our TechSkills Accelerator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In March last year, Daniel began work at IHiS as a front-end developer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He has contributed to two IT projects supporting the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Now, he is developing the user-facing components of the system supporting the One-Rehab framework, which I will speak a little bit more about later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope that more people will see opportunities in this HealthTech space and embrace the possibility that with some training, they can join the healthcare family, not necessarily as a clinician but contributing to the success of our public healthcare eco-system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, our early, comprehensive and persistent contact tracing and quarantine efforts have played a key role in our COVID-19 response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Besides the vigilance and skill of our healthcare workforce, our digital tools such as SafeEntry and TraceTogether continue to be central to the speed and efficiency of our contact tracing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Coupled with our aggressive testing strategies, these measures have contributed to our success in keeping the number of our community cases under control, for now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To swiftly identify COVID-19 cases and contain the outbreak, we have built up our testing capacity and our community testing operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through targeted operations as well as routine surveillance testing, such as the testing of our hawker centre workers, we have so far been able to detect cases and quickly prevent spread.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Healthcare professionals can access NEHR for their patients' COVID-19 test results and their existing medical conditions before the vaccination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The NEHR has also been enhanced this year to meet the requirements for COVID-19 vaccinations, displaying alerts and reporting problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We expect to complete most of this within the year and onboard more healthcare institutions to contribute to NEHR more securely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond COVID-19, we must be ready to respond to future public health crises by having the right systems and capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we will enhance our surveillance and response capabilities through the use of new technologies to enable us to more effectively consolidate, analyse and generate insights from large amounts of data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Second, we will augment our human capabilities to prepare Singapore against future threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Skilled clinical teams will always play an important role in detecting and managing new diseases and outbreaks, and we also need other experts such as epidemiologists, data scientists, statisticians and software engineers like Daniel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need teams to investigate and perform advance analytics, for example, to determine the likelihood of spread and inform our response to an outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will include (a) strengthening infectious disease collaboration networks locally and regionally; (b) strengthening capabilities for the accelerated development of diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines; and (c) establishing a national infectious disease repository and database for research and data analysis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To further address Mr Ang’s question, MOH regularly reviews our national response and is conducting an interim review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond pandemics, we must ensure that the healthcare needs of our general population are met.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our polyclinics are a vital element in our Public Health primary response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Built in 1980, Clementi Polyclinic is one of our oldest and smaller polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked whether we have considered patient’s comfort and staff’s performance in our design of healthcare facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When designing new healthcare facilities, the design team will engage stakeholders including the care team, patients and carers, and the facilities management team.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The redeveloped Clementi Polyclinic will undergo the same process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will be more spacious with more elderly-friendly and accessibility features.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Residents can also look forward to a comprehensive range of primary care services, including medical treatment for acute conditions, chronic disease management, women’s and children’s health services, as well as radiological, laboratory and pharmacy services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Another example of the on-going work to improve routine clinical care services despite the pandemic is to ensure our population has timely access to the right level of rehabilitation care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under this framework, patients will have improved access to community-based rehabilitation and benefit from expanded capacity and capability in the care providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our hospitals, polyclinics and community care providers will embark on a multi-year pilot to validate this new care model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our hope for patients with stable musculoskeletal conditions such as lower back pain who do not require surgery or complex interventions to receive this rehabilitation care in the community, instead of only at specialist clinics or hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: During last week’s Budget debate, we heard Dr Shahira Abdullah, Ms Carrie Tan, Dr Wan Rizal, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Mr Eric Chua speak about mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since the launch of the Community Mental Health Masterplan in 2012, and its enhancement in 2017, we have increased the capacity of community mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are on track to meeting our targets by end 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To Dr Wan Rizal’s question on support for youth and their families, we have piloted the Integrated Youth Service (IYS) within the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) and Care Corner, which is one of our community partners in the North.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In November 2020, the Care Corner team moved into the new Woods Square Community Space, to provide face-to-face mental health screening and basic emotional support sessions for persons with mental health challenges, and to conduct experiential resilience or mental well-being events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH and AIC have also worked with other community partners to set up youth community outreach teams to reach out to young people in mental distress to provide basic emotional support and resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The team would also engage the family to understand the stressors and the home environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Links to social and health services would also be provided.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through the Youth Mental Well-being Network, we have heard from the youth, mental health and social sector professionals, patients and caregivers, on how we could improve the mental well-being of our young people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling earlier shared on how the Network has initiated ideas for over 30 potential ground-up projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will also be sharing about an initiative to provide positive peer support during his MSF speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The three of us are working together, just as MOE, MSF and MSH are working together on this important area.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To look into the psycho-social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the population, we set up the COVID-19 Mental Wellness Taskforce in October 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond COVID-19, we will evolve the Taskforce into an inter-agency platform on mental health and well-being, by mid 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The platform will oversee mental health and well-being efforts, focusing on cross-cutting issues that require multi- and inter-agency collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are working out the details of the platform and will share more when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam asked about the support for other vulnerable groups such as our seniors and building a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government recognises that those who suffer from mental health conditions may face discrimination.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have been working with partners to roll out initiatives to address this issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will take a whole-of-society approach to tackle this issue effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The National Council of Social Service launched the “Beyond the Label” movement in 2018 to fight the stigma of mental health conditions and encourage social inclusion, positive attitudes and support towards persons living with mental health conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The movement also provides a platform for more conversations about mental health and promotes greater awareness and the acceptance of mental health conditions among the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To reach out to persons with or at-risk of mental health conditions or dementia, including seniors, community teams also reach out to residents and their caregivers to provide mental health or dementia information, basic emotional support and links to appropriate services, health or social, as necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For seniors at risk of social isolation, the AACs, Silver Generation Office and local grassroots organisations connect them to befrienders who will reach out to them on a regular basis, providing companionship and encourage them to participate in social activities, keeping active and keeping connected with the local community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Seniors can also sign up with CareLine, which is a 24/7 social support hotline that provides tele-befriending services as well as emergency response to seniors in distress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: While we do all this to build up the capabilities in our community partners, we will make sure that our main psychiatric sector, IMH, is updated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since 2018, IMH has been undergoing refurbishment and improvement works to facilitate the care and improve operational efficiency and safety for patients and staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And these works are expected to be completed by the end of 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, to fight COVID-19 we have had to rely on the skill, dedication and professionalism of our people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have had to develop and deploy technology and we have had to scale up clinical services, all the while looking after the many healthcare issues that are unrelated to the pandemic, but essential to our health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have had to be agile, steadfast and determined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are all a bit tired and fatigued, but also hopeful and confident that we can find our way forward.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, we remain committed to our long-term priorities even as we focus on containing the pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We continue to transform from Beyond Healthcare to Health, to support Singaporeans to lead healthier lifestyles and stay healthy in the “new normal”.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is important to take stock of our state of health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: However, based on our National Population Health Survey 2020, there are still areas for improvement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The proportion of Singaporeans that are obese or overweight has increased.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: And the age-standardised prevalence of the three common chronic diseases, high blood pressure and high blood cholesterol have risen and the prevalence of diabetes have not decreased.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There is a need to better understand the current situation among different groups.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Additionally, COVID-19 and the various measures and socio-economic challenges have impacted our lifestyles and our health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam has also asked about supporting healthy living in this new norm.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I will therefore share our plans to innovate health promotion efforts for Singaporeans to remain healthy in the “new normal” and how to better prepare Singaporeans to lead healthy lives for the future.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Indeed, in the past year, Singaporeans faced challenges pursuing healthier habits in ways they were used to.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With safe distancing concerns, we were unable to hold our usual health promotion programmes such as mass exercises.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As working from home became the norm, we also observed a drop in physical activity time, likely from reduced commuting.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This drop is also demonstrated in the daily average step count data from the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) National Steps Challenge.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We quickly pivoted to delivering our programmes virtually, in line with the safe management measures, or SMMs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We shifted physical activity programmes online, and produced exercise routines on YouTube and an edutainment series on free-to-air TV channels to help Singaporeans keep active.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand that some seniors have found it challenging to adapt from physical to virtual modes of exercise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To help seniors navigate around these platforms, we worked with partners such as People’s Association to organise workshops to provide assistance, and equip them with basic IT skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am heartened to hear that our regular participants have benefitted.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To benefit as many as possible given the current guidelines, we will be scaling up our virtual programmes progressively this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand that some still prefer physical interaction for health programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To reach out to more Singaporeans, we have gradually resumed physical sessions both in the community, such as our popular Sundays at the Park, and at the workplaces with the appropriate SMMs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Like physical health, mental wellbeing is also important for one’s health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I echo Senior Minister of State Janil on creating a supportive environment to empower Singaporeans to take care of their mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In August last year, we launched the “Brave the New” campaign with MCCY to build psychological resilience of individuals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To complement this, the “Hi!JustCheckingIn” movement started in January this year to equip targeted segments of the population with the appropriate skills to help them identify and reach out to those who may need support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Building a supportive community is important, to encourage Singaporeans to seek help if they are unable to cope.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through our community partners, we included seniors in our mental well-being efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand that many seniors are mentally and physically affected during this pandemic, especially during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, we trialled the virtual “Balik Kampung” programme to link up 100 seniors over 22 Senior Activity Centres over activities to stay mentally stimulated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With good feedback on how it has helped seniors stay socially connected, we will ramp up these efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The sixth season will start in the third quarter of this year and will augment the traditional Steps Challenge with a different dimension of well-being – sleep, via the first pilot Sleep Challenge.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Having good sleep habits is key to good health and well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through the Healthy365 application and a wearable, there will be nudges to achieve the recommended sleep duration, and tips on good sleep habits.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Interested participants can look out for more details on Healthy365 and HealthHub.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to work on avenues for Singaporeans to keep healthy while staying safe.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We recognise that at different life stages, Singaporeans face different health needs, challenges and risks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Going forward, we will add a person-centric approach to address these across our population segments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam has highlighted health literacy in her Budget debate speech and Dr Lim Wee Kiak has also suggested boosting our efforts with technology.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have embarked on initiatives similar to Dr Lim's vision.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Another example is LumiHealth, a free, two-year personalised health programme designed by HPB, in partnership with Apple, using the Apple Watch.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Under this programme, participants will embark on customised health journeys and earn rewards as they complete health-related challenges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: They will also receive personalised reminders, to encourage them to meet their goals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We must also not forget our efforts to keep chronic conditions at bay, like our on-going War on Diabetes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH developed the Patient Empowerment for Self-Care Framework to empower patients to co-own their care journeys and achieve better care outcomes with support from their healthcare team, family and friends.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Under this framework, we developed the first tranche of the National Diabetes Reference Materials that provides fundamental information and hosted it online on HealthHub.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are now working on the next tranche of materials with more in-depth information to help patients, their family and friends, better understand and manage diabetes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This resource is being co-created by the people for the people – about 700 citizens highlighted additional topics and content that would be useful, and suggested design features for a more user-friendly online experience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond our broad plans for our Singaporeans, I will elaborate on targeted efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Leon Perera has highlighted the lower income groups.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Minister Gan has shared how we ensure they have good access to affordable care.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: While our health promotion efforts remain inclusive to all, there are also efforts targeted to address their health needs, and we work across agencies to provide holistic support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: One example is the Healthy Living Passport programme, which Mr Perera referred to.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The programme is designed to improve health literacy and promote healthy lifestyles.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is customised based on the lifestyle needs of lower income families, with tailored messaging and education.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We intend to track changes in our participants' health literacy as well as their behavourial improvements.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This would allow us to evaluate the impact of our programmes as we generally do with our efforts.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We see significant disparities in health behaviours and outcomes across ethnicities and will be ramping up efforts in this area.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
